name: Market Breadth
rationale: Breadth rules test whether internal market participation improves timing compared with price-only signals.
expected_benefit: Potential earlier risk-off or risk-on signals when index price hides weak participation.
failure_modes: Breadth data may be hard to source and validate.
Signals may be noisy and threshold-sensitive.
Index constituent changes can create survivorship problems.

canonical_variants.name: Advance/decline filter
canonical_variants.description: Hold equity exposure only when advance/decline breadth is healthy.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: An advance/decline breadth filter may reduce equity exposure before broad market declines.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 75% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Percent-above-MA filter
canonical_variants.description: Use percentage of constituents above a moving average as a market health signal.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A percent-above-moving-average breadth filter may improve drawdown control versus index-price-only filters.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown more than the comparable price-only filter without worse CAGR retention.

canonical_variants.name: New-high/new-low filter
canonical_variants.description: Use the balance of new highs and new lows as a risk signal.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A new-high/new-low breadth filter may identify fragile markets before index drawdowns become large.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative and improve Sharpe.

suggested_validation: Do not proceed without data provenance and survivorship notes.
Compare to a price-only regime filter.
Use long histories if the data is reliable.
execution_notes: The current engine does not support external breadth series.
